result.title: LOCI: Localized Continuous Control for Multi-Subject Image Editing
result.summary: Recent instruction-following image editors such as Flux.1-Kontext enable text-driven editing but lack fine-grained control over where and how much an edit is applied. Existing approaches provide either continuous but global control or spatially localized editing at a fixed strength. To our knowledge, none jointly supports explicit spatial localization, continuous per-region strength, and independent simultaneous control of multiple subjects. We present LOCI (LOcalized Continuous control for multi- subject Image editing). Given a multi-subject image with per-subject regions and instructions, LOCI edits each subject at an independently chosen, continuously adjustable strength, for instance gradually aging one person while adding a beard to another with minimal cross-region leakage. LOCI pairs subject-level attention binding for spatial isolation with a Regional LoRA layer that replaces the LoRA's scalar coefficient with a per-token scaling vector aligned to the spatial layout. A single adapter is trained at one suppression point, and continuous edit strengths follow by rescaling its regional residual at inference. Experiments on multi-subject scenes demonstrate that LOCI achieves strong edit fidelity with significantly reduced cross-region interference compared to baselines, while maintaining continuous control over edit strength

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LOCI 多主体图像编辑方法：用主体级 attention binding 实现空间隔离，并以 Regional LoRA 把 LoRA 的标量系数替换为与空间布局对齐的 per-token 缩放向量，只在单一强度点训练，推理时缩放区域残差得到连续可调编辑强度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按空间布局对 token 加权、连续调节区域残差」的机制，可能与 LVR 中区域化视觉证据筛选、局部 latent 状态的强度控制存在方法上的可借鉴之处，值得核查；但论文本身属图像编辑，未涉及推理过程或 latent 推理状态。
